title: Logs
description: Every log line the fleet ships, and the line rate that says whether anything is arriving at all. Filter by machine, container, level and a substring. No panel here serves an alert: the counts the log error and silence rules evaluate are charted on the Fleet health board, in its log rules row.

panels.title: Total lines/min
panels.description: Is anything arriving at all? One line, every selected stream summed — the transport canary. A flat zero here while the fleet is otherwise healthy means the shipping path is down, not that the fleet went quiet. Context panel: no alert evaluates this expression, so it carries no threshold line — the silence rules and the count each of them computes are charted on the Fleet health board, in its log rules row. Counted per minute; the shipping paths here are low-volume by design, so a healthy total is a small number.

panels.title: Last line seen — per stream
panels.description: A rate of zero and a stream that never existed render identically on a graph; this table tells them apart. One row per stream that has shipped at least one line in the last twenty-six hours — the widest window any log rule evaluates — carrying the wall-clock time of that line. A row present with an old timestamp is a stream that has gone quiet. **A row missing while other rows are present** is a stream already past every rule's patience; streams that exist on only one machine are expected to be missing from the other, and the edge machine ships metrics only, so it never appears here at all. **An entirely empty table means something different, and never that the whole fleet went silent.** Unless the pickers are narrowed to the edge machine alone, or to a container none of the selected machines runs, no rows at all means this panel's own query failed — a broken panel, not a verdict. Read the line rate to its left before you treat anything as an outage: it answers the same question through a different query, and if it shows lines arriving then this table is the thing that is wrong. Context panel, carrying no threshold of its own — the silence rules' pages land on the Fleet health board's silence-rule chart, which holds each rule's own count.

targets.expr: max by (host, container) (max_over_time({host=~"$host", container=~"$container"} | label_format seen=`{{ unixEpoch __timestamp__ }}` | unwrap seen [26h])) * 1000

panels.title: Logs — $container / $level
panels.description: Every line, newest first, shown as its message, parsed here at query time; the stored line is unchanged. A line with a message key shows that message with any stack trace beneath it, a line with a msg key its logger or source location, its message and its error, and any other line shows as it was collected. Level is a real stream label on every path, so filtering and colouring work the same way for all of them. Expand a row to see every key the parse read out of the line.

targets.expr: {host=~"$host", container=~"$container", level=~"$level"} |= "$search" | json | logfmt | drop __error__, __error_details__ | line_format "{{ if .message }}{{ .message }}{{ if .exception }}\n{{ .exception }}{{ end }}{{ else if .msg }}{{ if .logger }}{{ .logger }} - {{ else if .caller }}[{{ .caller }}] - {{ end }}{{ .msg }}{{ if .error }}: {{ .error }}{{ else if .err }}: {{ .err }}{{ end }}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}"

list.name: host
list.label: Host
list.query: Capture primary : zcrypto, Capture secondary : zcrypto-red, Ops : ops, NAS : nas, Edge : zaccess, Cache 1 : zcrypto-valkey1, Cache 2 : zcrypto-valkey2, Cache 3 : zcrypto-valkey3, Monitor : zcrypto-mon, Dead-man : zcrypto-hc
list.description: Which machines the panels below select. All expands to the pinned machines joined into one matcher — the option list is the pin, so a stray label value cannot appear here. The edge machine ships metrics only and no log lines at all, so selecting it on its own empties every panel on this board by construction rather than by fault. The monitor and dead-man machines ship their log lines to the monitor's own Loki alone, so on Grafana Cloud selecting either on its own empties this board the same way. This list is a second place to edit when a machine joins the fleet.

list.name: container
list.label: Container
list.description: Container or unit that produced the line. The names are not symmetric across machines: the archive-pull loop appears in this list as `archive-pull` on the NAS and as `zcrypto-archive-pull` on the ops machine, so picking one of them silently blanks the other machine. Leave it on All unless you are chasing a single stream. The list is read when the board loads and when the machine picker changes, not on every refresh, so a container that started shipping after the page loaded appears here after a reload.

list.name: level
list.label: Level
list.description: Log level, carried as a real stream label on both paths — set by the shipping agent for the streams it collects, and by the daemon itself for the ones that push straight to the log store. Multi-select; All stays a match-anything pattern on purpose, so lines that carry no level label at all — the pull loop's own shell output — still appear. The list is read when the board loads and when the machine or container picker changes, not on every refresh, so a level first shipped after the page loaded appears here after a reload.

list.name: search
list.label: Search
list.description: Case-sensitive substring filter on the log line (leave empty for all).
